terms.comment: Our phrase: Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no term for automated testing. Probātiō is the lexicon’s word for testing (see testing). Automatus is self-moving, spontaneous (Petr. 50.1, Lewis & Short), and the modern works use it of machines that work by themselves: an automatic rifle is sclopētum automatum (Traupman 371) and a motorcycle birota automata (M-O s.v. bicycle: motorcycle). Testing by hand is probātiō manuālis (see manual testing).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 371.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. bicycle: motorcycle.
